items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. items.title: From possession conditions to the genesis of concepts: Peacocke and Cognitive Psychiatry
items.summary: Christopher Peacocke proposed that a concept is individuated by the conditions a subject must meet to possess it, bringing the philosophy of concepts closer to cognition, but he left unexplained how those conditions arise. This article aims to propose, from the standpoint of Cognitive Psychiatry, a genetic and communicational theory of conceptualization that completes Peacocke’s theory of possession conditions. It is a theoretical proposal essay supported by a narrative review of recent literature (2021–2026) in philosophy of mind, cognitive science, developmental psychology and neuroscience.

items.title: Autism as Developmental Constraint Reconfiguration
items.summary: Autism is conventionally framed as a neurodevelopmental spectrum defined by differences in social communication, restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviour, and atypical sensory processing. While this clinical description is indispensable, it does not by itself specify the systems-level architecture that makes such a phenotype possible. items.title: Cognitive Psychiatry and the genesis of knowledge: From Meno’s paradox to cosmogenetic analyticity
items.summary: Arthur Pap’s functional a priori explains how laws change function once knowledge is constituted, but not how the conceptual core enabling such change is formed. items.summary: Abstract The reward positivity (RewP) is an event-related brain potential (ERP) component associated with feedback and goal completion. Although the component is said to be generated in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), this inference is disputed because of the inverse problem. Recent intracranial electroencephalogram (EEG) current source density analyses provided direct evidence that the RewP is generated in caudal ACC, specifically Brodmann areas 24c’ and 32’. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests
